llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed China A-share data and technical-analysis helper, with no evidence of hidden persistence, credential theft, destructive behavior, or exfiltration.

dimensions.detail: Runtime behavior is proportionate for a financial data skill: it imports BaoStock, pandas, numpy, and local MyTT code, queries public market data, and prints reports; no local private files, credentials, or account data are accessed.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation uses pip packages baostock and pandas with minimum-version constraints rather than pinned versions, which is a reproducibility and supply-chain hygiene issue but not evidence of malicious behavior.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill documents automatic technical analysis for explicit 'technical side' requests and requires confirmation before full-market scans; it does produce trading-style suggestions, so users should treat outputs as informational only.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No cron jobs, services, shell profile edits, memory writes, privilege escalation, destructive commands, or background persistence were found; documentation examples include CSV export, but the bundled scripts do not persist data.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The main purpose is BaoStock market-data access, and the bundled MyTT technical-analysis script is related and disclosed in SKILL.md, though the front-matter description should mention analysis more clearly.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with a Chinese-language A-share data skill that queries BaoStock and may produce technical-analysis opinions. Treat any buy/sell-style output as informational, verify data independently, and consider pinning dependencies before use.
llm.findings:
[TP2] expected: The mixed Chinese and ASCII name reflects a Chinese-language BaoStock skill name, not a deceptive tool-spoofing pattern in the inspected artifact.
[TP4] expected: The scanner's mismatch concern is partly downgraded because SKILL.md and _meta.json disclose MyTT/technical-analysis functionality; the front matter is incomplete but the behavior remains finance-purpose aligned.
[SDI-1] expected: Technical analysis and CSV examples are broader than pure data retrieval, but they are visible in the documentation and related to market-data use.
[SQP-1] expected: The trigger is broad, but it is tied to explicit technical-analysis wording and does not grant hidden or privileged authority.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The RSI labels are a correctness concern because RSI(6), RSI(12), and RSI(24) are all sourced from the same RSI output; this affects analysis quality, not agent security.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The script prints recommendation-like investment language without a clear disclaimer; this is an important user-risk issue but not evidence of malicious behavior or unauthorized action.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese-only text is expected for an A-share/BaoStock-focused skill, though clearer locale disclosure would improve usability.
[SC1] unexpected: Unpinned baostock and pandas dependencies are a real supply-chain hygiene weakness, but no malicious dependency source or install-time execution was found in the artifact.
[SC4] unexpected: The pandas advisory signal is low-confidence and unresolved because versions are not pinned; this supports dependency guidance rather than escalation.
